title: Private Observability Minimum Pack — Kickoff Notes (working)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working kickoff notes for “Private observability minimum pack” (VPC + on-prem). Capture goals, initial proposal for dashboards/alerts/log pipeline, owners, early risks/open questions.
- This is not the final PRD; we’ll link back to PM-842 and the Confluence overview once published.

Meeting(s)
- Kickoff: 2025-05-14 10:00–11:00 PT
- Follow-up (metrics/labels): 2025-05-20 09:30–10:15 PT

Attendees (kickoff)
- Product: Vivek Kulkarni
- Program: Talia Benson
- Platform/Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Private Deployments: Diego Santos
- Control Plane: Ethan Park
- SRE/Obs: Neha Kapoor, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant
- Dashboards/Tooling: Dylan Brooks
- Security: Marcus Lin
- SE/On-prem constraints: Fatima Noor
- Support readiness: Dev Patel

One-liner / definition we aligned on
- “Minimum supported pack” = the baseline set of metrics + dashboards + alerts + log pipeline defaults that ship with Private installer/Helm and are supported by Redwood Support/SRE without bespoke customer setup.
- We are standardizing “day-2 visibility” (health/perf/correctness signals) and reducing escalations caused by missing/fragile observability.

Non-goals (explicitly called out)
- No ‘premium’ long-retention / federated multi-cluster / heavy customization in v1.
- No requirement to deploy a full tracing backend for v1 (we’ll keep traces “where feasible” and focus on metrics + logs).
- We are not building a SIEM; we provide export/forwarding to customer tools.

Success criteria (initial)
- Private install (VPC and on-prem-like air-gapped) can be validated with a deterministic checklist:
  - Prometheus scrapes all Redwood targets successfully.
  - Grafana dashboards render and show non-zero traffic when sending synthetic requests.
  - At least one alert can be triggered via failure-injection (e.g., stop runtime pods / block scrapes) and surfaces with correct annotations + runbook links.
  - Logs are structured, redacted by default, and export examples work (at least 2 sinks validated).
- Support can use the runbooks to resolve top 5 observed issues without engineering escalation.

Scope inventory — components that must emit signals in v1
- Data plane:
  - Serving runtime pods (request/latency/token throughput/batching/kv cache/gpu/mem)
  - Router/policy engine (routing decisions, fallback counts, request queueing/backpressure)
- Control plane:
  - API gateway
  - Auth/RBAC integration points (as metrics only; no sensitive logging)
  - Model registry integration points (fetch failures, version resolution, cache hits/misses)
  - Installer/upgrade controller (jobs, upgrade state transitions, failures)

Decision points (tentative; track in ADRs)
- Metrics/alerts stack: assume Prometheus-compatible metrics + Grafana dashboards (customer may already have Prom/Grafana; we ship our “observability-pack” assets + Helm wiring).
- Logging stack: ship default collector config (to be decided: promtail/vector/fluent-bit) with structured JSON parsing + redaction; provide sinks (Loki/ELK/Splunk/OTLP) as supported configurations.
- Cardinality policy: we must bound label cardinality for customer clusters; avoid raw tenant_id, request_id as labels; model/route labeling must be capped/aggregated.

Workstreams + initial owners
1) Requirements + ‘minimum supported’ definition
- Owner: Vivek Kulkarni
- Inputs: Support top incidents, SE constraints, SRE paging requirements
- Output: acceptance criteria + versioning policy + what’s “supported vs best-effort”

2) Metrics inventory + naming/cardinality standards
- Owners: Nadia Rahman + Thomas Baird (perf/cardinality)
- Support: Allison Grant (standards)
- Output: list of required metrics, allowed label sets, and backward-compat/migration plan

3) Dashboards bundle (Grafana)
- Owners: Dylan Brooks (integration) + Sergio Costa (authoring) + Chloe Martin (packaging)
- Output: versioned bundle in observability-pack + dashboard catalog page

4) Alerts + recording rules
- Owners: Neha Kapoor + Aisha Bello
- Output: baseline recording rules + alert rules with severity taxonomy + tuned thresholds + runbook links in annotations

5) Logging pipeline defaults + export matrix
- Owners: Logan Wright + Colin O’Donnell
- Security reviewers: Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei
- Output: default collector config + redaction guidance + validated configs for at least Splunk HEC + Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (OTLP optional in v1)

6) Installer/Helm wiring + offline packaging
- Owners: Diego Santos + Connor O’Brien
- On-prem validation: Fatima Noor
- Output: Helm values toggles, preflight checks, postinstall validation, offline bundle manifest includes dashboards/rules/configs

7) Validation + smoke tests
- Owners: Sahana Iyer + Leila Farouk
- SRE validation: Rafael Mendes
- Output: e2e harness, failure injection checks, upgrade/rollback validation

Candidate dashboards (v1 “must have” list)
A) Runtime Overview (Private)
- Golden signals: RPS, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (by route group), in-flight, saturation
- Token metrics: tokens/s, prompt vs completion tokens, time-to-first-token (if available)
- Batching/KV cache: batch size distribution, queue wait, cache hit/miss, kv cache utilization
- GPU: utilization, memory used, OOM events, throttling indicators
- Pod health: restarts, CPU/mem, node placement
Owner: Omar El-Sayed (metrics) + Sergio Costa (dashboard)

B) Control Plane Health
- API gateway: request rate, 4xx/5xx, auth failures, upstream latency
- Policy/routing: decision latency, fallback counts, error types
- Model registry integration: fetch latency, failures, cache hit rate
- Installer/upgrade controller: job statuses, reconcile errors, time in state
Owner: Ethan Park + Sergio Costa

C) Cluster / Infra (minimum subset)
- Prometheus scrape health (targets up, scrape duration, sample ingestion)
- TSDB health (disk usage, head block churn, compactions) — may be “recommended” but we should surface it
- Grafana health (datasource errors, query errors)
Owner: Neha Kapoor + Rafael Mendes

D) Logs pipeline health (collector)
- Log collector CPU/mem, queue/buffer utilization, dropped logs, retries, sink errors
Owner: Logan Wright

Dashboard notes
- We should keep dashboard count low; preference is ~4–6 “minimum pack” dashboards with strong navigation links.
- Each panel must document “what good looks like” + likely failure modes.
- Avoid high-cardinality template variables (model/route) as default. If included, must be bounded and/or use top-k.

Candidate alert rules (v1 initial list)
Principles (aligned with SRE)
- Page only on symptoms + imminent customer impact (availability, latency SLO burn, total scrape loss).
- Ticket-only for early warnings (disk pressure, moderate saturation, noisy-but-actionable).
- All alerts require: clear summary, severity, runbook link, and “first 3 steps”.

A) Availability / request failures
- API availability: 5xx rate above threshold or error budget burn rate high
- Router/policy engine errors spiking
- Runtime error rate (non-2xx) sustained
Owner: Neha Kapoor + Aisha Bello

B) Latency SLO burn
- p95/p99 latency burn rate (fast + slow burn multiwindow)
- time-to-first-token regression (if metric exists; else defer)
Owner: Aisha Bello

C) Saturation / resource pressure
- GPU utilization sustained near max (with queueing increase) — warning
- GPU memory near max + OOM killed containers — page if OOM kill loops
- CPU/memory pressure causing throttling / restarts
- Pod restart loop (CrashLoopBackOff) on runtime/router/control-plane
Owner: Rafael Mendes

D) Queueing / backpressure
- Queue depth above threshold and increasing
- Request drop/429 due to overload sustained (warning → ticket)
Owner: Omar El-Sayed

E) Observability stack health (must have for supportability)
- Prometheus target down for Redwood critical components
- Grafana datasource errors sustained
- Log collector dropping logs / sink auth failures sustained
Owner: Neha Kapoor + Logan Wright

Logging (v1 proposal)
- Structured logs (JSON) for control plane + data plane.
- Fields we want consistently (subject to security review):
  - timestamp, level, service, component, pod/node, cluster_id
  - request_id (in logs only; DO NOT use as metric label)
  - route (consider bucketing/allowlist), model (consider bucketing/allowlist)
  - tenant_id_hash (salted hash; logs only; no raw tenant id)
  - error_code / error_type
- Default redaction: strip/replace tokens and known secret patterns; do not log prompt/completion payload by default.
- Default retention guidance (placeholder): keep operational logs 7–14 days in-cluster unless customer exports; audit logs are separate (per Security policy).
- Export targets (prioritized):
  - Splunk HEC (common enterprise ask)
  - Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
  - Loki (if customer wants in-cluster)
  - OTLP logs (nice-to-have; depends on collector choice)

Installer/Helm expectations
- Installer must support:
  - Preflight checks (PVC/storage class, resource requests, network policy assumptions for scrapes)
  - Postinstall validation (“are targets up? do dashboards exist? can we query basic metrics?”)
  - Offline/air-gapped: bundle MUST include dashboards + alert rules + collector config + images; checksums in manifest
- Helm values toggles:
  - enable/disable dashboards import, alert rules, log collector
  - retention knobs (Prometheus + logs), resource requests/limits
  - export sink configs (disabled by default; docs show examples)

Early risks / gotchas (captured live)
1) Metric cardinality explosions
- Biggest risk is labels: route/model/tenant. Private clusters often smaller; Prometheus can fall over if we ship hosted-style cardinality.
- Action: require standards doc + instrumentation changes where needed; provide aggregated metrics + top-k views.

2) Air-gapped packaging drift
- Known failure mode: offline bundle missing dashboards/rules or wrong versions.
- Action: single “observability pack” artifact version + bundle manifest verification + CI test that installs without internet.

3) Alert noise / paging hygiene
- Thresholds that work in hosted don’t translate to small private footprints (bursty traffic → false positives).
- Action: multiwindow burn rate alerts + defaults that are conservative; some alerts disabled by default (ticket-only) until tuned.

4) Grafana datasource auth + namespaces
- Customers have custom Grafana deployments / locked-down namespaces. Our dashboards must not assume hardcoded datasource names or namespaces.
- Action: dashboard provisioning that references datasource UID via values; document required RBAC.

5) NetworkPolicies block scrapes
- Private customers frequently lock down egress/ingress; Prometheus can’t scrape targets.
- Action: installer preflight detects common NP patterns; docs include minimal NP rules; provide “scrape diagnostics” runbook.

6) Security review of logs
- Need explicit agreement on not logging payloads; watch for accidental inclusion via debug logs.
- Action: security sign-off on log schema; unit tests or linting for prohibited fields.

Open questions (need decisions)
- Collector choice: vector vs fluent-bit vs promtail (criteria: ease of config, resource usage, sink support, airgap friendliness).
- OTLP: do we require OTLP exporter support in v1 or treat as “best effort” (customer demand vs schedule)?
- Do we ship a “minimal Prometheus/Grafana” deployment as part of installer, or only ship assets + wiring for customers who already run them? (Current leaning: assets + wiring; optional reference deployment documented.)
- How do we version dashboard/rule bundles across Private releases? (Need: backward-compat or explicit migration steps.)

Next 2 weeks (action items)
- Vivek: finalize definition + acceptance criteria for “supported minimum” (PM-842 update).
- Nadia/Thomas/Allison: draft required metrics + label allowlist + cardinality constraints; propose recording rules list.
- Sergio/Dylan: start dashboard skeletons (runtime + control plane) using bounded template variables.
- Neha/Aisha: propose initial alert rule set with severities + which are enabled by default.
- Logan/Colin/Marcus: pick log collector candidate + draft redaction guidance; list required sinks.
- Diego/Connor/Fatima: draft installer preflight list + offline bundle manifest requirements.
- Sahana/Leila/Rafael: outline smoke test plan (install, scrape, dashboard render, alert fire, offline install).

Notes-to-self / reminders (program)
- Keep Confluence as “source of truth” once we converge; Drive doc is fine for messy iteration.
- Ensure every alert includes runbook link (oncall feedback from past incidents).
- Build a “known issues” list early (dashboards empty, scrape blocked, log sink auth errors) and route to Support enablement.

Appendix: strawman timeline (rough)
- Wk 1–2: requirements + inventory + standards
- Wk 3–4: dashboard/alerts/log pipeline implementation begins
- Wk 5–6: Helm/installer wiring + offline packaging
- Wk 7–8: validation + smoke tests + failure injection
- Wk 9: support enablement + release notes + GA checklist
